6.5 Temperature (normal)
6.5.1  
Appliances shall not, at any point, attain a temperature sufficiently high to constitute a fire hazard or to
affect adversely any materials used in the equipment; nor shall they show temperatures at specific
points greater than those indicated in Table 2, based on an ambient temperature of 25°C, except that
the temperature of snow movers shall be based on an ambient temperature of 0°C. The test conditions
shall be either
a) 
under normal load as described in Clause 6.2; or
b) 
operated continuously until constant temperatures are obtained while loaded (by eddy current
dynomometer or by clamping the blades together.

<!-- 第 35 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
6.5.2  
Temperature tests may be conducted at any room temperature between 0 and 40°C, and the variation
below or above the ambient temperature specified in Clause 6.5.1 shall be respectively subtracted from
or added to the permitted limiting temperatures specified in Table 2.
6.5.3  
Temperature readings shall be obtained by means of thermocouples, or coil temperatures may be
determined by the rise of resistance method, or other suitable methods as described in CSA C22.2 No.
100. A temperature shall be considered constant when three successive readings, taken at intervals of
10% of the previously elapsed duration of the test but not less than 5 min, indicate no change.
6.5.4  
The limiting temperature for insulating materials other than those given in Table 2 shall be the subject
of investigation.
6.5.5  
Equipment shall also meet the requirements of Clause 6.5.1 when tested at the extreme operating
voltages of the supply system (see CSA CAN3-C235), e.g., at 104 and 127 V, while operating in the
intended manner at any speed setting, with an additional allowance of 20°C above the specified
insulation temperature limits for a 120 V nominal system voltage.
6.6 Dielectric strength
6.6.1  
Immediately after the temperature test, the equipment shall withstand at room temperature for a
period of 1 min, without breakdown, the application of an ac voltage of 50 or 60 Hz between live parts
and non-current-carrying conductive parts that may become grounded, as follows:
a) 
1000 V for machines of any rated voltage from 31 to 250 V; and
b) 
500 V for extra-low voltage circuits (other than self-generating millivolt circuits) at 30 V or less.
Solid state control circuits, which normally have a connection to ground, may have the ground
connection disconnected during the dielectric test.
6.6.2  
An appliance that can cut into or contact concealed live wires shall withstand without breakdown for
one minute the application of a 60 Hz essentially sinusoidal potential of 1250 V between the insulating
grasping surfaces of the appliance and accessible dead metal surfaces which may become energized.
6.6.3  
Compliance with the requirements of Clause 6.6.1 shall be determined by means of a suitable testing
transformer, the output of which can be regulated. Starting at zero, the applied voltage shall be
increased gradually and at a uniform rate either until the required test value is reached or breakdown
occurs.
6.6.4  
For this test, all switches and controls shall be in the ON position.

<!-- 第 36 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
6.7 Leakage current
6.7.1  
At the discretion of the manufacturer, the leakage current test required by Clause 4.20 may be
performed using new samples for each test. The tests shall be performed under the following
conditions:
a) 
as received; and
b) 
after humidity conditioning in the humidity chamber; leakage current measurements shall be
performed after the appliance has been subjected for 48 h to a moist atmosphere having a relative
humidity of 80 W 90% at a temperature of 32 ± 2°C.
6.7.2  
The meter may be electronic or a direct indicating type, average responding, calibrated at 60 Hz and
indicating the rms value of a pure sine wave, with an accuracy of 5% at an indication of 0.5 mA. The
meter shall have a terminal impedance of 1500 Ω shunted by a 0.15 μF capacitor.
6.7.3  
The test circuit shall be as shown in Figure 6.
6.7.4  
The equipment shall be at room temperature with all appliance switches in the ON position and switch
S1 open; it shall be tested within 5 s of applying the test voltage (switch S1 closed) and again after
reaching normal operating temperatures. Equipment with speed or temperature controls shall be tested
at the low, medium, and high settings of the controls.
6.7.5  
The tests shall be conducted first with switch S2 in position A and then in position B, and then with
switch S1 both closed and open.
6.7.6  
The grounding conductor of cord-connected equipment that has a grounding circuit shall not be
connected to ground except through the test meter.
6.7.7  
Equipment having an enclosure of insulating material shall have the probe, after it has been applied to
metal foil with an area of 100 x 200 mm, placed in contact with accessible surfaces of insulating
material.
6.8 Water test
6.8.1  
An appliance shall be brought into the focal area of the three spray heads specified in Clause 6.8.2, in
such a position so that water will be most likely to contact the live parts. The following shall apply:
a) 
Ground-supported appliances shall be in their normal at-rest position.
b) 
Hand-held appliances shall be placed on a hard, flat, level surface in a position that allows the
appliance to support itself.

<!-- 第 37 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
c) 
Appliances shall be conditioned for 1 h as follows:
i) 
Appliances intended to be operated in rain or snow shall be water-conditioned both while
operating and while not operating. Appliances conditioned while operating shall be
conditioned in their normal operating position.
ii)
Appliances not intended to be exposed to rain or snow shall be conditioned while not
operating.
d) 
Immediately following the water conditioning in Item (c) and before the tests, as specified in
Clause 6.8.3, an appliance that has been conditioned while not operating shall be rotated to permit
accumulated water to drain.
6.8.2  
The water spray apparatus used for the conditioning test of Clause 6.8.1(c) shall consist of three rain
test spray heads mounted in a water supply pipe rack as illustrated in Figure 20. The spray heads shall
be constructed in accordance with the details specified in Figure 19. The water pressure for all tests
shall be maintained at 34 kPa at each spray head. The distance between the centre nozzle and the
appliance shall be approximately 1.5 m. The spray shall be directed at an angle of 45° to the vertical,
towards the louvres or other openings nearest the current-carrying parts. The following shall apply:
a) 
At the submittor's request, the water used for the conditioning shall have its resistivity adjusted
(before the test is started) to 3500 Ωcm at ±5% when measured at 25°C.
b) 
At the conclusion of the test the resistivity of the water shall be not less than 3200 or more than
3800 Ωcm at 25°C.
6.8.3  
After exposure to the water conditioning described in Clauses 6.8.1(c) and 6.8.2, an appliance
a) 
rated for a nominal 120 V supply shall comply with the requirement in Clause 6.7 in a repeated
leakage current test, except that the test shall be discontinued when the leakage current stabilizes;
or
b) 
of a type other than that mentioned in Item (a) shall have an insulation resistance of not less than
50 000 Ω between live parts and interconnected non-current-carrying metal parts; and
c) 
shall withstand without breakdown for 1 min the application of a 60 Hz, essentially sinusoidal
potential between live parts and exposed non-current-carrying metal parts. The dielectric test
potential shall be
i) 
1000 V for grounded appliances;
ii)
2500 V for double insulated appliances rated at nominal 120; or
iii) 3500 V plus twice the rated voltage of the appliance, for a double-insulated appliance that is
rated at more than a nominal 120 V.
6.9 Performance of manually operated switches
6.9.1 Overload
6.9.1.1
Switches shall be tested at the specified test voltage (see Clause 6.1.2) and the rated frequency of the
appliance, by making and breaking the stalled motor current 50 consecutive times without undue
arcing, burning, pitting, or welding of the switch contacts, and without either electrical or mechanical
failure. If, in addition to the motor, another circuit is controlled by the switch, it shall also be included in
the test load.

<!-- 第 38 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
6.9.1.2
The following test conditions shall be complied with:
a) 
The duration of the ON and OFF periods shall be such that the temperature rise of the motor
windings does not exceed that normally encountered in service. The switches shall not be operated
at a rate faster than 10 times per minute.
b) 
Those switch poles that are least liable to arc to non-current-carrying metal parts shall be
connected to such parts through a suitable fuse. Under this condition the fuse shall not open.
6.9.1.3
If the equipment has both an ac and a dc rating, the test specified in Clause 6.9.1.1 shall be conducted
with the equipment connected to a dc supply of the maximum rated voltage, and the dc overload test
shall be considered representative of the test for ac. In the event that the switches fail to pass the dc
tests but subsequent samples pass the ac tests, the equipment shall be rated for ac use only.
6.9.2 Endurance
Switches shall comply with the endurance test required by CSA C22.2 Nos. 55 or 111, as applicable,
except that the rated load may be considered to be the load controlled by the switch in the equipment.
6.10 Stability
The stability of a mower or snow mover shall be such that all wheels or skids will maintain their position
on a surface inclined 15° from the horizontal. A mower that is intended to be operated with or without
a grass catcher shall be tested with and without the catcher attached.
6.11 Flame test
Plastic enclosures and supports that are required to have flame retardant coatings, liners, etc, to meet
the requirements of the flame test shall be tested with the parts, or a specimen, as required, in both
the received (new) condition and (with additional samples) after the following conditioning:
a) 
Samples shall be placed in a circulating air oven for 100 h at the specified continuous temperature
rating of the plastic as determined by ASTM D648 at 66 psi or at 10°C above the maximum
temperature occurring on the material during the normal temperature test in Clause 6.5,
whichever is the lower; but in no case shall this temperature be less than 90°C.
After the heating cycle the samples shall be removed from the oven and placed for 30 min in a
refrigerator held at a temperature of –30 ± 2°C.
b) 
The heating and cooling cycles in Item (a) shall be repeated twice more.
c) 
After the third heating and cooling cycle the samples shall be conditioned for 24 h at 32 ± 2°C and
a relative humidity of 80–90%.
6.12 Flexing
6.12.1
The power supply cord and interconnecting cords that are flexed during use shall withstand a flexing
test of 20 000 cycles, where the cord enters the enclosure, without causing exposure or breakage of the
conductors, or displacement or breakage of the antikink device, if supplied. The rate of flexing shall be
10 cycles/min unless the manufacturer agrees to a faster rate. The flexing test may be performed on a
different sample than the one used for the strain relief test.

<!-- 第 39 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
6.12.2
One cycle of the flexing test shall consist of the movement of the cord from one position of the most
extreme flex to the opposite position of the most extreme flex and back again, but no more than a total
of 180° (twice), and in the direction resulting in the most severe test.
6.12.3
The flexing test shall be conducted with the cord under a tension of 1.1 N, when the tension is applied
to the cord 200 mm from the point of cord entry.
6.12.4
At the completion of the test, the appliance shall withstand the dielectric strength test specified in
Clause 6.6 and shall still function.
6.12.5
There shall be no impairment of the strain relief as determined by the tests specified in Clause 6.13.
6.13 Strain relief
Strain relief for power supply cords shall prevent the transmission of strain to terminations when
a) 
a steady pull of 158 N is applied in any direction for 1 min;
b) 
the cord is pushed in, in which case the cord shall be prevented from contacting sharp edges,
points, or moving parts, or exposure to temperatures above the temperature rating of the cord
insulation; or
c) 
a 0.353 Nm torque is applied at 25 mm from the strain relief for 1 min.
6.14 Physical abuse
6.14.1
Appliances shall withstand the abuse tests specified in Clauses 6.14.2 to 6.14.5 without affecting the
mechanical safety and electric shock protection features provided. An appliance shall be considered to
comply with this requirement if on completion of the tests it complies with all of the following items:
a) 
there are no cracks or openings that cause bare live parts to be accessible to the probes as
specified in Clause 4.3.4;
b) 
the appliance meets the leakage current requirement of Clause 6.7;
c) 
there is no reduction of the guarding (see Clause 4.3.3); and
d) 
there is no cracking of the electrical enclosure if a dust-tight or weatherproof enclosure is required.
6.14.2
Appliances that are hand held during use (excluding hedge trimmers), shall have one sample dropped
three times onto a concrete surface from a height of 1 m. The sample shall be positioned to vary the
point of impact.
The points of impact shall be those most likely to produce adverse results.
6.14.3
Chain saws shall withstand a single impact of 1.4 J applied through a 6.35 mm diameter steel sphere to
the brush cap or in the area of the brush cap.

<!-- 第 40 页 -->

Motor-operated gardening appliances
6.14.4
The actuating mechanism of chain saw switches and controls shall be subjected to three impacts of 1.4 J
each, applied through a 6.35 mm diameter steel sphere.
6.14.5
Ground supported appliances such as mowers, edgers, edger trimmers, cultivators, and snow movers
shall be subjected to three impacts of 6.8 J from a solid steel sphere 50.8 mm in diameter and weighing
approximately 0.54 kg, dropped through a distance of 1300 mm while the equipment is supported on a
rigid surface. Each impact shall be at a different location and shall be applied on any surface that is
exposed to a blow during normal use.
For other than a horizontal surface the steel sphere shall be suspended and permitted to fall as a
pendulum through the required (vertical) distance before striking the point of impact. For snow movers
with polymeric components, this test shall be performed after conditioning the appliance for a
minimum of 4 h at –35 ± 2°C.
6.14.6 Rotary mowers
6.14.6.1
The blade drive fastening means shall be given a torque test as follows:
a) 
the blade shaft shall be locked;
b) 
the blade or blade support shall have a torque applied in the direction of rotation until the torque
reaches 68 Nm on the shaft or the blade has turned 15 revolutions; and
c) 
the blade or blade support shall have a torque applied in the opposite direction until the torque
reaches 68 Nm or the blade has turned 15 revolutions on the shaft.
The results of the test shall not show any evidence of failure, and the initial value of the torque of the
blade fastening means shall not have been reduced by more than 10% after the 15 revolutions.
6.14.6.2 Blade unbalance test
6.14.6.2.1
A mower shall be operated for 1 h with a blade made unbalanced by adding or removing weight to
result in an unbalance, U, as determined by the following formula:
where
LI
=I the diameter of the blade tip circle,
Each blade of a multiblade mower shall be tested separately. A new mower may be used for testing
each blade
6.14.6.2.2 Test arrangement
The test arrangement shall be as specified in Clause 6.14.6.4.2.
6.14.6.2.3
Failure of this test shall be indicated by any of the following:
a) 
barrier penetration by any part of the mower; or

b) 
evidence of fracture, loosening, or deformation anywhere in or on the mower that results in a
hazard to the operator or bystanders.
6.14.6.3 Structural integrity test
6.14.6.3.1 Blade enclosure and guards
The blade enclosure and guards of a mower shall be tested as follows:
a) 
Test procedure—one hundred hardened steel balls, 12.7 mm in diameter (minimum Rockwell C
scale 45) shall be introduced in an upwards vertical direction, one at a time through two or more
equally spaced holes for each blade. The balls shall be divided into approximately equal quantities
among the holes. The test shall be conducted one time for each blade assembly. At the discretion
of the manufacturer, a new mower housing or mower attachment may be used for each blade of
multiblade mowers.
b) 
Test arrangement—the test arrangement shall be as specified in Clause 6.14.6.5.2.
c) 
Test acceptance—the mower shall be deemed acceptable when
i) 
there is no penetration by more than 1/2 of any ball through any surface; and
ii)
any part of the housing guard or associated grass catcher breaks off or bends, but the mower
complies with Clause 6.14.6.5.
6.14.6.3.2 Grass catcher
A grass catcher provided by the mower manufacturer for use with a mower shall be tested as follows. A
catcher that is designed for use on more than one type of mower shall be tested for each application.
a) 
Test procedure
i) 
The mower test arrangement and procedures shall be as specified in Clauses 6.14.6.5.2 and
6.14.6.3.1(a), with a grass catcher mounted on the mower.
ii)
A bystander target shall be provided as indicated in Figures 8 to 12 for each test. For
multiblade mowers, this test shall be performed for only the blades nearest the discharge
openings.
iii) Any openings between the bottom panel and the lower edge of the grass catcher shall be
closed.
iv) An additional panel of 350 lb Mullen test, double-wall corrugated paper board shall be placed
to delineate the mower side of the operator zone, as indicated in Figure 13. This target shall
extend from the ground level of the mower upwards to a height of 2.13 m. If the target is less
than 0.5 m from any part of the grass catcher, the target may be repositioned at that location
to maintain a separation of 0.5 m.
v) 
At the discretion of the manufacturer a new mower or mower attachment may be used for
each set of the following tests:
1) 
A ball test as specified in Clause 6.14.6.3.1 shall be performed prior to the nail test and
shall be performed for each discharge opening for which a grass catcher is provided.
2) 
A nail test shall be performed identically to the ball test except that it shall consist of the
upward vertical introduction of 200 (sixpenny) 2 in common steel nails, one at a time,
headfirst. The test shall be performed with the same catcher and mower.
3) 
The nails used for this test shall be bright common round wire nails. The nails shall be
free of flash and unusually sharp edges from shearing or clamping during the
manufacturing process.
b) 
Test acceptance
The grass catcher shall be deemed acceptable when none of the following occur:
i) 
penetration of the bystander target;

<!-- 第 42 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
ii)
any strike or penetration of the operator zone target;
iii) any opening of a zipper or bag seam, or
iv) the grass catcher dislodges from its adapter or falls from its normal position.
A grass catcher complying with this test shall be deemed to comply with Clause 6.14.6.5.
6.14.6.4 Sudden impact test
6.14.6.4.1
The cutting blade of rotary mowers shall be subjected to a sudden impact with a 25.4 mm diameter
steel rod within 50 mm of the blade tip circle. The blade shall be rotating at maximum speed at the time
of impact (See Figure 10).
The mower shall be stationary at the time, held with resilient restraints if necessary, and with the
blade(s) set for a cutting height of 50 mm.
Each blade of a multiblade mower shall be tested separately. A new mower may be used for testing
each blade.
6.14.6.4.2 Test arrangement
The entire mower shall be housed centrally in a rectangular barrier consisting of 350 lb Mullen test,
double wall corrugated paper on four sides and the top. There shall be no more than 610 mm
clearance, at each side and the top, between the inside of the corrugated barrier and the nearest part
of a complete lawn mower, less the handle. The corrugated paper shall be supported along the outside
edges to maintain stability during the test. Minimum openings for sufficient motor cooling shall be
provided. The test(s) shall be conducted with the blade(s) properly assembled on a complete mower.
6.14.6.4.3
The results of this test shall be acceptable if there is
a) 
no barrier penetration by any part of the mower;
b) 
no breakage of the blade; and
c) 
no breakage of the blade vertical retention means to the blade driving shafts.
6.14.6.5 Thrown object test—Discharge opening(s)
6.14.6.5.1 Test procedure
The test procedure shall be as follows:
a) 
This test shall consist of the upward vertical introduction of 300 (sixpenny) 2 in common steel nails,
one at a time, headfirst through each of two equally spaced holes.
b) 
The mower or mower attachment shall be tested for each discharge opening using the test
arrangement of Clause 6.14.6.5.2, with the mower or mower attachment and the target positioned
as shown in Figures 8 to 13.
c) 
In addition, the bottom panel shall be relieved in the area defined by lines tangent to the first hole,
extending to the intersection of the discharge chute and the outer wall of the mower housing.
(Refer to the shaded areas shown in Figures 8 to 13).
d) 
For multiblade mowers this test shall be performed only for the blade(s) nearest the discharge
opening(s) and any other blade having a greater horizontal angle of discharge.

<!-- 第 43 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
6.14.6.5.2 Test arrangement
Note: See Figures 10 to 15.
The test arrangement shall be as follows:
a) 
The mower or mower attachment shall be equipped with a 19 mm plywood panel, which shall be
faced with a steel plate of at least 16 gauge thickness for wear resistance, parallel to and 16 mm
below the horizontal plane of the blade. The panel shall extend a minimum of 25 mm beyond the
blade tip circle at the discharge opening(s).
b) 
An air inlet hole with a diameter that is approximately 30% of the blade length shall be provided in
the panel concentric with each blade tip circle; on mulching mowers only, the concentric air inlet
opening of the mower support fixture may be increased to a diameter up to 80% of the blade
length, provided that a minimum overlap of 25 mm is maintained between the edge of the
injection opening periphery and the edge of the concentric air inlet opening.
c) 
The opening between the lower edge of the mower housing and the panel shall be closed except
at the discharge opening(s).
d) 
The holes in the test panel for the introduction of the test material shall be 25 mm in diameter and
generally equally spaced from the primary hole, which shall be located 45° back of a radial line
drawn through A, the centre point of the discharge opening, as shown in Figures 8 to 13.
e) 
The angular location of the other holes may be varied slightly to avoid interferences with the
structural components or the test equipment.
f) 
The test material shall be injected with sufficient energy that it will rise a minimum of 13 mm and a
maximum of 305 mm, if unobstructed, above the horizontal plane of the blade.
g) 
Spring, air, or other assists may be used to ensure proper introduction of the test material. When a
tube is used to introduce the test material through the holes, the end of the tube should be 51 mm
below the horizontal plane of the blade in order to permit the test material to emerge freely from
the tube.
6.14.6.5.3 Test acceptance
a) 
Bystander target — not more than 15% of the nails introduced into the mower shall strike or
penetrate the bystander target above the horizontal plane of the blade(s) and not more than 0.5%
shall strike or penetrate the bystander target above a line 610 mm above the horizontal plane of
the blade(s).
b) 
Operator zone target — none of the nails introduced into the mower shall strike or penetrate the
operator zone target.
6.14.6.6 Handle structure
For determining compliance with Clause 4.17.8, the mower shall be positioned on a horizontal
supporting surface and restrained from any movement at the wheels or blade enclosure. A static force
of 222 N shall be applied to the grasping part of the handle, in the most leveraged operating position on
the longitudinal centre line of the mower, in a direction towards the front of the mower and parallel to
the supporting surface.
6.14.7 Snow movers
6.14.7.1
Snow movers shall withstand the tests specified in Clauses 6.14.7.2 to 6.14.7.4 while the appliance is
operating at the maximum intended speed, without resulting in any hazardous condition, mechanical or
electrical, to the operator or bystanders.

The appliance shall withstand, while operating at maximum speed, running into a vertical concrete wall

perpendicular to the wall;

6.14.7.3
The tests specified in Clause 6.14.7 shall be performed after conditioning the appliance for a minimum

A snow mover shall be operated for 1 h, or until the appliance no longer operates, with its impeller

There shall be no evidence of fracture, loosening, or deformation anywhere in or on the snow mover

6.15 Blade stopping
Compliance with Clause 4.17.6 shall be determined by running the appliance for 6 min to ensure
stabilized operating conditions at maximum speed. The appliance shall be turned off and the time from
the turning off action until the blade or impellor comes to a stop shall be measured.
6.16 Speed control — Limited short circuit test
6.16.1
Each of six controls shall be connected in turn to a circuit limited as specified in Table 3 at a power
factor of 0.9–1.0. The circuit capacity shall be measured without the control or protective fuse in the
circuit.
6.16.2
Each control to be tested shall be connected in the circuit in series, with the power supply cord, where
applicable, supplied with the equipment and a nonrenewable (not of the time delay type) fuse that is
four times the full load current of the motor, as determined in Clause 6.2, but not less than 15 A.
6.16.3
The enclosure and exposed non-current-carrying metal parts surrounding the control shall be grounded
and surgical cotton shall be placed in and around all the openings of the enclosure.

<!-- 第 45 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
6.16.4
The six samples shall be tested by closing the short circuit on each speed control. Three samples shall be
tested with the control set at the maximum speed and three samples with the control set at the
minimum speed.
6.16.5
In each case there shall be no ignition of the cotton.
6.17 Temperature (abnormal)
6.17.1
When operated under abnormal conditions, equipment shall be considered a hazard if the probe
specified in Clause 4.3.4 can contact live parts, bare or insulated.
6.17.2
To determine if a hazard actually exists, a separate burn-out or abnormal heating test shall be
conducted, with the rotor of the motor stalled, and with the equipment connected to an electrical
supply circuit and operating continuously until the ultimate result has been determined. The following
test conditions shall be complied with:
a) 
The equipment shall be located or supported as for the normal temperature test.
b) 
Controls such as temperature-regulating thermostats shall be set at their maximum heat position.
6.17.3
The equipment may be stationary during the test, and the conditions of operation need not
approximate those of actual service.
6.17.4
The ultimate result may be constant temperatures, the opening of the circuit by a fuse or a thermal
protector, or the opening of a winding without resulting in a hazard.
6.17.5
The appliance shall also withstand the dielectric strength test described in Clause 6.6, after the
abnormal temperature tests.
6.17.6
Appliances incorporating a one-shot fusible device shall, in addition, be tested by subjecting five
samples to a stalled rotor test.
6.17.7
In addition to the test of Clause 6.17.2, the starter motor of a gasoline engine shall also be tested by
continuously cranking the unit for 1 min immediately following the normal temperature test.
6.18 Foot probe test
6.18.1 Test conditions
The following test conditions shall be met:
a) 
This test shall be performed on a smooth level surface.

<!-- 第 46 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
b) 
Pneumatic tires, when present, shall be inflated to the cold pressures recommended by the mower
manufacturer.
c) 
The mower housing shall be adjusted to its highest setting relative to the ground.
d) 
The blade shall be adjusted to its lowest position relative to the blade housing.
e) 
The mower shall be secured so that it may not move horizontally but is free to move vertically.
6.18.2 Areas to be probed
The areas to be probed shall include the following:
a) 
An area both 60° to the right and 60° to the left of the rear of the fore-aft centreline of the cutting
width.
i) 
For single blade mowers, these angles shall be measured from a point on this fore-aft
centreline that is at the centre of the blade tip circle (see Figure 14).
ii)
For multiblade mowers, these angles shall be measured from a point on the fore-aft centreline
of the cutting width that is one-half of the cutting width forward of the rearmost point of the
composite of all the blade tip circles (see Figure 15).
b) 
For a mower with a swing-over handle, the areas to be probed shall be determined, in the same
manner as in Item (a), from both possible rear positions (see Figure 16).
c) 
Where a 360° foot protective shield is required, the entire periphery of the mower shall be probed
(including any discharge chute comprising part of the periphery).
d) 
When the foot probe of Figure 3 is inserted under any point within the areas to be probed during
this foot probe test, the shields shall prevent the foot probe from entering the path of the blade or
causing any part of the mower to enter the path of the blade.
6.18.3 Procedure
Within the areas specified, the foot probe of Figure 3 shall be inserted under the bottom edge of the
blade housing and shields. During each insertion, the sole of the probe shall be kept in contact with the
supporting surface. Insertion shall stop when the mower housing lifts or the horizontal force used to
insert the probe reaches 18 N, whichever occurs first. As the foot probe is withdrawn after each
insertion, the toe shall be pivoted upward around the heel as much as possible without lifting the
mower. The entire foot probe shall remain within the 60° lines to the right and left of the rear of the
fore-aft centreline of the cutting width.
Note: For this test the mower should be disconnected and rotated manually.
6.19 Moisture absorption—Insulating materials
Insulating material, where required by Clause 4.9, shall not absorb more than 10% of water by mass,
when immersed in distilled water for 24 h at a temperature of 23 ± 1°C. The material shall be
conditioned at 105 ± 3°C for 1 h before weighing and immersion.
7 Requirements for cord-connected double-insulated appliances
7.1 General
7.1.1  
This Clause is supplementary to, or amendatory of, those requirements given elsewhere in this
Standard. It forms the basis for the design and construction of cord-connected appliances that have
double insulation in lieu of the grounding of exposed non-current-carrying conductive parts, if any, and
that are marked to indicate this in accordance with Clause 7.4.

<!-- 第 47 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
7.1.2  
These requirements shall apply to cord-connected equipment on circuits not exceeding 150 V to ground
for use in nonhazardous locations, and designed to be used in accordance with the Rules of the
Canadian Electrical Code, Part I.
7.2 General requirements
7.2.1  
Double-insulated appliances shall not have provision for grounding.
7.2.2  
The construction shall be such that the failure of two independent sections of insulation must occur
before any exposed metal can become alive, unless the construction is such that reinforced insulation is
acceptable (see the definition of “double-insulated appliance” in Clause 3).
7.2.3  
Reinforced insulation shall be used only when it is manifestly impracticable to use double insulation.
7.2.4  
Supplementary insulation shall provide insulating and mechanical properties that are not less than
those of the functional insulation normally acceptable for the appliance.
7.2.5  
Where a part or the whole of the enclosure is of insulating material (i.e., there is no exposed metal), it
shall be treated as supplementary insulation or reinforced insulation.
7.2.6  
Functional insulation and metal insulated from bare live parts by functional insulation shall not be
accessible to the user, as required by Clause 7.3.2.2.
7.2.7  
Capacitors shall not be connected to exposed conductive parts.
7.2.8  
The construction shall be such that normal use of the appliance, including servicing, will not result in the
loss of insulation as originally provided.
7.3 Construction
7.3.1 General
7.3.1.1
Except where reinforced insulation is used, supplementary insulation shall be interposed between all
exposed non-current-carrying conductive parts and
a) 
functionally insulated current-carrying parts including insulated wire; and

<!-- 第 48 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
b) 
non-current-carrying conductive parts that are separated from bare current-carrying parts by
functional insulation.
Note: A permanently maintained air space may be accepted as either supplementary or reinforced insulation.
7.3.1.2
The construction shall be such that the added protection provided by any additional insulation will not
be reduced by the normal use and servicing to which the appliance is liable to be subjected.
7.3.1.3
Unless protected from physical abuse by the outer enclosure of the appliance or by other means,
supplementary insulation shall be adequately resistant to such abuse.
Note: Supplementary insulation that comprises the outer enclosure of the appliance is considered to be adequately
resistant to physical abuse if the appliance complies with the mechanical strength requirements of Clause 6.14.
7.3.1.4
At a switch having its own enclosure of insulating material, reinforced insulation shall be acceptable in
place of double insulation if all of the following conditions are met:
a) 
all live parts of the switch, other than terminals, shall be completely enclosed in the switch
enclosure;
b) 
no dead metal part that extends outside the switch enclosure shall enter the arc chamber;
c) 
a plunger, toggle, or the like that contacts live parts shall be made wholly of insulating material;
d) 
with the exposed external parts of the plunger, toggle, or the like removed, no live part inside the
switch enclosure shall be accessible, and no live part inside the switch enclosure shall be contacted
by the actuating arm, cam, or the like;
e) 
the metal mounting screws or rivets by which the switch is secured to the accessible dead metal of
the tool shall not pass through the body of the switch enclosure but may pass through tabs, ears,
or other projections from the switch body, including a piece of insulating material secured to the
switch; and
f) 
a portion of a switch or switch enclosure that contains arcing parts and that may therefore be
subjected to arcing shall be separated from the exposed dead metal of the appliance by mica not
less than 0.127 mm thick or by other insulation having equivalent properties. Metal switch
assembly screws, rivets, clamps, or other devices that pass through or around the body of the
switch enclosure shall be suitably insulated from the dead metal to which the switch is secured.
7.3.2 Openings and recesses
7.3.2.1
There shall be no openings other than those that are required for the proper functioning of the
appliance, including the dissipation of the heat generated during its normal operation.
7.3.2.2
Openings or recesses that allow access to bare live parts, functionally insulated parts, or functional
insulation shall be of such size or shape that they will prevent the entry of Probe 1 as shown in Figure 4,
inserted to only length L.
Note: Magnet (e.g., film coated) wire is considered to be a bare live part for the purposes of this requirement.

<!-- 第 49 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
7.3.2.3
Openings, including construction joints, shall be designed to minimize the accumulation of dirt or
fragments of metal and commutator dust, which could cause bridging or serious contamination of
insulating surfaces.
7.3.3 Mechanical assembly
7.3.3.1
Bare live parts shall be so constructed and secured that in normal use they cannot come into contact
with supplementary insulation or non-current-carrying conductive parts that are separated from
external conductive parts by only supplementary insulation.
7.3.3.2
The construction shall be such that an air gap between such parts cannot be reduced to below the value
permitted or easily bridged by foreign matter.
7.3.3.3
The construction shall be such that it will prevent wires, screws, nuts, washers, springs, and similar
parts, which might become loose or free, from bridging supplementary or reinforced insulation. Only
one part shall be considered as loosening or becoming free at any one time.
7.3.3.4
Sleeves, if provided as supplementary insulation on insulated conductors, shall be secured in position to
prevent their accidental removal (e.g., during servicing).
7.3.3.5
An accessible brush cap shall be
a) 
of suitable insulating material;
b) 
recessed so that its top is behind the plane of the brush holder opening in the surrounding portion
of the enclosure of the appliance; and
c) 
capable of withstanding three impact tests as specified in Clause 6.14.3, each impact being made
on a different part or area of the enclosure, without cracking or exposing bare live parts.
7.3.4 Supply connection
7.3.4.1
The power supply cord shall have a mechanical serviceability of at least that required for grounded
appliances, and shall not have a grounding conductor.
7.3.4.2
The power supply cord shall be additionally insulated from exposed conductive parts at the point where
it enters the appliance.
Note: A jacket on a cord is not considered as supplementary insulation.
7.3.4.3
A metal strain relief clamp shall not be accessible and shall not make contact with an accessible non-
current-carrying conductive part unless the clamp is suitably insulated from the cord.

<!-- 第 50 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
7.3.5 Spacings
7.3.5.1
The spacings shall be not less than those specified in Table 4, except that larger spacings may be
required at points at which carbon dust, lubricants, or other conductive contaminants exist or may
accumulate.
7.3.5.2
Magnet (i.e., film coated) wire shall be considered a bare live part in determining compliance with the
spacings specified in Table 4.
7.3.5.3
When spacings are measured, screws that are not prevented from loosening shall be positioned, by
unscrewing if necessary, to produce minimum spacings.
7.3.5.4
All over-surface spacings shall be measured along or across the joints unless these joints are effectively
cemented together.
7.3.5.5
Spacings measured through openings in the housings of insulating material shall be measured from
metal foil drawn tightly across the opening.
7.3.5.6
All air gaps shall be included in determining over-surface spacings, except those less than 1.016 mm
wide.
7.3.5.7
The depth of any groove less than 1.016 mm wide shall not be considered in determining the over-
surface spacing.
7.4 Marking
Appliances conforming to these requirements shall be marked in accordance with the requirements for
double-insulated equipment specified in CAN/CSA-C22.2 No. 0.
7.5 Tests
7.5.1 Dielectric strength
While at normal operating temperature, the appliance shall be capable of withstanding, without
breakdown, for a period of 1 min, the application of the ac test voltages of 50 or 60 Hz specified in
Table 5 (See also Clause 6.8.3).

<!-- 第 51 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
7.5.2 Leakage current
7.5.2.1
When tested under the conditions specified in Clauses 7.5.2.2 to 7.5.2.4, the leakage current, measured
with a resistance of 1500 Ω connected in the circuit and with the appliance at normal operating
temperature, shall not exceed
a) 
3.5 mA with the nominal system voltage specified in CSA CAN3-C235 (e.g., 120 V) applied between
each side of the supply circuit, in turn, and the inaccessible functionally insulated non-current-
carrying conductive parts; and
b) 
0.5 mA with the nominal system voltage applied between each side of the supply circuit, in turn,
and the exposed non-current-carrying conductive parts, or metal foil 10 x 20 cm in area or smaller
if total area is less than 200 cm2, that are in contact with the external nonconductive surfaces.
7.5.2.2
Prior to measuring the leakage current, the sample shall be operated under no load conditions for 100 h
or until the brushes wear out, whichever interval is shorter, but in no case for less than 25 h.
For a double-insulated starter motor, the motor shall be operated under no load at a duty cycle of 5 s
ON and 3.5 min OFF, or a shorter OFF time at the discretion of the manufacturer, for a total ON time
of 1 h.
Note: The brushes may be replaced during this test.
7.5.2.3
Following the no load (conditioning) test specified in Clause 7.5.2.2 and prior to measuring the leakage
current, the sample shall be subjected for 48 h to a moist atmosphere having a relative humidity of
80–90% at a temperature of 32 ± 2°C.
7.5.2.4
The test frequency shall be rated hertz or dc, whichever is applicable.
7.5.3 Supplementary insulation test
7.5.3.1
Severe overstress of the functional insulation shall not cause the failure of the supplementary insulation
as determined by
a) 
the leakage current test specified in Clause 7.5.2.1(b) monitored while the unit is still hot; and
b) 
the dielectric strength test specified in Clause 7.5.3.4. Nor shall severe overstress cause bare or
functionally insulated live parts to be exposed, as specified in Clause 7.3.2.
7.5.3.2
To determine compliance with the requirements of Clause 7.5.3.1, a motor-operated appliance shall be
subjected to a running overload test. While it is connected to a fused 30 A branch circuit of nominal
system voltage, by operating the appliance at full load for a period of 30 min and increasing the load by
10% every 30 min until any one of the following conditions occurs:
a) 
the 30 A fuse blows;
b) 
the input current suddenly increases by 100%, or more, of rated current;
c) 
flame appears (if flame occurs it shall be extinguished immediately); or
d) 
there is an open circuit in the motor winding(s).

<!-- 第 52 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
7.5.3.3 Protector
7.5.3.3.1
During the test specified in Clause 7.5.3.2, any protective device, provided with the appliance, that can
be reset, replaced, repaired, or otherwise modified by the user, shall be short-circuited.
Note: The objective of the test is to determine the integrity of the appliance insulation and not the effectiveness of
a protective device, other than a thermal cutoff type as specified in Clause 7.5.3.3.2.
7.5.3.3.2
A one-shot nonresettable or nonreplaceable thermal cutoff that is permanently embedded in the motor
may be used to limit the end result of the test as specified in Clause 7.5.3.2 if opening the thermal
cutoff renders each motor part it is intended to protect permanently inoperative and requires that
these parts be replaced in order to return the appliance to a functional condition.
7.5.3.4
Following the test specified in Clause 7.5.3.2, the appliance shall be given time to cool to room
temperature. The appliance shall then be capable of withstanding, without breakdown, for a period of
1 min, the application of an ac voltage of 1000 V between the live parts and the accessible non-current-
carrying conductive parts or metal foil as specified in Clause 6.7.7.

Annex A
Safe operation practices for walk-behind mowers
Note: This Appendix is not a mandatory part of this Standard.
A.1 . Safety instructions
A.1.1 Training
The following should be carried out for training:
a) 
Read the operating and service instruction manual carefully. Be thoroughly familiar with the
controls and the proper use of the equipment.
b) 
Never allow children to operate a power mower.
c) 
Keep the area of operation clear of all persons, particularly small children, and pets.
d) 
Do not use a mower for any job except that for which it is intended.
A.1.2 Preparation
The following preparations should be carried out:
a) 
Thoroughly inspect the area where the equipment is to be used and remove all stones, sticks,
wires, bones, and other foreign objects.
b) 
Do not operate the equipment when barefoot or wearing open sandals. Always wear substantial
footwear.
c) 
Disengage the self-propelled mechanism or drive clutch on units so equipped before starting the
motor.
d) 
Never attempt to make a wheel height adjustment while the motor is running.
e) 
Mow only in daylight or in good artificial light.
f) 
Never operate the equipment on wet grass. Always be sure of your footing; keep a firm hold on
the handle and walk, never run.
A.1.3 Operation
During operation, the following should be observed:
a) 
Do not put hands or feet near or under rotating parts. Keep clear of the discharge opening at all
times.
b) 
Stop the blade(s) when crossing gravel drives, walks, or roads.
c) 
After striking a foreign object, stop the motor, unplug, thoroughly inspect the mower for any
damage, and repair the damage before restarting and operating the mower.
d) 
If the equipment should start to vibrate abnormally, stop the motor and check immediately for the
cause. Vibration is generally a warning of trouble.
e) 
Stop the motor and unplug whenever leaving the equipment, before cleaning the mower housing,
and before making any repairs or inspections.
f) 
Shut the motor off and wait until the blade comes to a complete stop before removing the grass
catcher or before unclogging the chute.
g) 
Mow across the face of slopes, never up and down. Exercise extreme caution when changing
direction on slopes. Do not mow excessively steep slopes.
h) 
Never operate the mower without proper guards, plates, or other safety protective devices in
place.
i) 
Do not wash with a hose; avoid getting water in motor and electrical connections.

<!-- 第 76 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
A.1.4 Maintenance
The following maintenance items should be carried out:
a) 
Check the blade and the engine mounting bolts at frequent intervals for proper tightness.
b) 
Keep all nuts, bolts, and screws tight to be sure the equipment is in safe working condition.
c) 
Check bag frequently for deterioration and wear, and replace worn bags. Check that replacement
bags comply with the original manufacturer's recommendations or specifications.
d) 
Replace the blade if it is bent or cracked. An unbalanced blade causes vibration that could damage
the motor drive unit or cause personal injury.
e) 
Sharpen a dull blade equally at each end to maintain the balance.
f) 
Clean the blade thoroughly and check its balance by supporting it horizontally on a thin nail
through its centre hole. The nail should also be in a horizontal position. If either end of the blade
rotates downward, remove some metal from the heavy or lower end until the blade is balanced. It
is balanced when neither end drops.

<!-- 第 77 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
Annex B (normative)
Safety instructions for saw chain pole pruners
Note: This Annex is a mandatory part of this Standard.
B.1  
The instruction manual shall include the following minimum information:
a) 
The following warning:
“WARNING – Do not operate near electrical power lines. The unit has not been designed to provide
protection from electric shock in the event of contact with overhead electric lines, Consult local
regulations for safe distances from overhead electric power lines and ensure that the operating
position is safe and secure before operating the saw chain pole pruner.”
and
« Attention: Ne pas opérer près des lignes électriques. L'unité n'a pas été conçue pour protéger
contre les chocs électriques en cas de contact avec les lignes électriques aériennes. Consulter la
réglementation locale pour les distances d'éloignement sécuritaires des lignes électriques
aériennes et s'assurer que la position de fonctionnement est sûre et sécurisée avant d'opérer
l'échenilloir à scie en chaîne. »
b) 
Description and identification of the principal parts of the saw chain pole pruner including the
safety devices and harness, and the use of the quick release mechanism.
c) 
Instruction for adjusting the proper tension of the saw chain, lubricating, maintenance, and for
transportation and storage.
d) 
Advice on correct working posture, maintaining firm footing and balance during operation
including the safe usage of the harness, the quick release mechanism, and the need for rest
periods and changing working position.
e) 
Advice of the need for hearing, head, and eye protection and the necessary PPE to be used
including correct clothing.
f) 
Advice on the risk for bystanders, especially for children, and the need to keep them at a safe
distance during the operation of the saw chain pole pruner.
B.2  
The instruction manual shall also include the following safety warnings:
a) 
Keep all parts of the body away from the saw chain. Make sure the switch is off when clearing
jammed material. Saw chain continues to move after the switch is turned off. A moment of
inattention while operating the extended-reach pruner may result in serious personal injury.
b) 
Carry the extended-reach pruner by the handle with the saw chain stopped. When transporting or
storing the extended-reach pruner, always fit the saw chain device cover. Proper handling of the
extended-reach pruner will reduce possible personal injury from the saw chain.
c) 
Hold the extended-reach pruner by insulated gripping surfaces only, because the saw chain may
contact hidden wiring or its own cord. A saw chain contacting a "live" wire may make exposed
metal parts of the extended-reach pruner "live" and could give the operator an electric shock.
d) 
Keep cable away from cutting area. During operation the cable may be hidden in shrubs and can be
accidentally cut by the saw chain.
e) 
Do not use the extended-reach pruner in bad weather conditions, especially when there is a risk of
lightning. This decreases the risk of being struck by lightning.
f) 
To reduce the risk of electrocution, never use near any electrical power lines. Contact with or use
near power lines may cause serious injury or electric shock resulting in death.

<!-- 第 78 页 -->
Copyrighted material licensed to Intertek. No further reproduction or distribution permitted.
Motor-operated gardening appliances
g) 
Always use two hands when operating the extended-reach pruner. Hold the extended-reach pruner
with both hands to avoid loss of control.
h) 
Always use head protection when operating the extended-reach pruner overhead. Falling debris
can result in serious personal injury.
Note: Alternate wording for "extended-reach" is possible, e.g. “pole” or “long reach”.

The International Standard CISPR 14-1 has been prepared by subcommittee CISPR/F:
Interference related to household appliances,tools, lighting equipment and similarappliances,
of IEC technical committee CISPR.
This sixth edition cancels and replaces the fifth edition published in 2005, Amendment 1:2008
and Amendment 2:2011. This edition constitutes a technical revision.
This edition includes the following significant changes with respect to the previous edition:
full editorial review of the standard, rearranging the structure of several clauses;
improvements to the operating conditions for testing induction cooking appliances and
incorporation of the limits for these appliances in the body of the standard;
-8 -
CISPR 14-1:2016 @ IEC 2016
moving all specific operating conditions to Annex A;
improvement of definitions;
addition of general and specific test setups (e.g. vacuum cleaners and robotic cleaners)
for radiated emission;
provision for the current probe test method for conducted disturbance measurements on
ports other than the AC mains port in alternative to the voltage probe method;
clarifications about click analysis (e.g. measurements under the presence of continuous
disturbances). Further clarification is being developed for future inclusion;
clarification about the use of the artificial hand;
CISPR 32 requirements);
clarification in the scope regarding emissions from radio transmitters (copied verbatim
from CISPR 32);
clarification about the measurement of equipment with built-in luminaries.

necessary,e.g.because the equipment has no source of disturbance,the equipment is
deemed to comply with the requirements without testing.

Artificial Mains Network (AMN)
Where this standard specifies the use of an AMN, the artificial mains V-network 5o Q2/50 μH
(or 50 Q2/50 μH + 5 2) as defined in Clause 4 of CISPR 16-1-2:2014 shall be used.
The connection between the AMN and the measuring receiver shall be made by means of a

During all measurements of disturbance voltage and disturbance current (on the mains port or

on associated ports) the mains port of the EUT shall be connected to the EUT port of an AMN

Where this standard specifies the use of a voltage probe, the device shall be as defined in 5.2
of CISPR 16-1-2:2014. If the impedance of the probe is too low, thus affecting the operation
of the EuT, more suitable values of its components shall be chosen (for example 15k2 in
series with 500 pF).
The readings shall be corrected according to the voltage division factor between the probe
and the measuring instrument set. For this correction factor, only the resistive parts of the
impedances shallbetakenintoaccount.
5.1.5
Current probe
The current probe shall be in accordance with 5.1 of CISPR 16-1-2:2014.

In order to simulate the influence of the user's hand, the application of the artificial hand is
required for hand held equipment during the disturbance voltage and disturbance current
measurement.

- 32 -
CISPR14-1:2016@IEC2016
It is generally considered that for frequencies above 3o MHz radio interference energy is
propagated by radiation. Experience has shown that the disturbing energy is mostly radiated
by the part of the mains leads and other leads near the EUT. It is therefore agreed to define
the disturbing capability of an EUT as the RF power it could supply to its leads. This power is
nearly equal to that transferred by the EUT to a suitable absorbing device (absorbing clamp)
placed around these leads at the position where the absorbed power is at its maximum.

5.3.4.3.1
General
The boundary of the EUT is defined by an imaginary circle encompassing the EUT. The centre
of this imaginary circle shall be at the same position as the centre of the turntable (see
Figure 12).
The distance from the receive antenna reference point to the boundary of the EuT shall be
the measurement distance as required by the limits used (see 4.3.4.5).
If ancillary equipment is needed to operate the EUT, this ancillary equipment is not part of the
EUT and its radiated emissions shall not influence the test results e.g. by placing it outside
the screened room.
Table-top EUT shall be placed at (0,8 ± 0,o5) m above the reference plane of the test site
selected for measurement (see Figure 13 and Figure 14).
Floor standing EUT shall be placed at (0,12 ± 0,04) m above the reference plane of the test
site selected formeasurement (see Figure 16).
Parts supporting the EUT and its parts at the required height shall be made of non-
conductive material.
Where the EUT comprises multiple parts, these shall be arranged to minimise, as far as it is
reasonably practical, the test volume. A minimum distance of o,1 m shall be maintained
between these parts (see Figure 17 and Figure 18).
shall be determined by referring to the basic standard relevant to the test method selected for
measurement.
5.3.4.3.2
Cables

===== 第 58 页 / 共 157 页 =====
All cables, both signal and power, are covered in this subclause.
Retractable cables on reel cords or in cable compartments shall be fully extracted and
bundled as appropriate.
For cables leaving the test volume:
Mains cables shall be routed directly from the EuT vertically to the floor (see Figure 13,
Figure 14, Figure 16, Figure 17 and Figure 18 as examples).
If more than one cable is connected to the EUT and leaves the test volume, then all other
cables shall be routed together with the nearest mains cable to the floor. These cables
shall be routed first down to the supporting surface and then around the periphery of the
EUT using the shortest possible path to the nearest mains cable (see Figure 15 as an
example).
At the point where each cable reaches the ground plane (or leaves the test volume in the
FAR) it shall be taken through a CMAD. Each cable shall be routed through a single
CMAD separately (see Figure 13 to Figure 18 as example). If more than three cables are
leaving the test volume only the mains cable(s) shall be routed through CMADs.
When measuring in a FAR, at least o,8m of cables leaving the test volume shall be visible
from the antenna reference point (see Figure 19).
For cables terminating within the test volume:

more than 2 dB in the 15 s period, then the disturbance measurement shall be performed in
accordance with the conditions of normal use of the equipment, as follows:

seconds, shall be ignored.

frequency range for which limits are specified.
Quasi-peak and average values shall be given for the significant maxima of the measured
Peak envelope (i.e. above or nearer the limit).
5.4.1.4
Where disturbance power is assessed, measurements shall be made throughout
the frequency range 30 MHz to 300 MHz.

5.4.3
Exceptionsfromtheclickdefinition
5.4.3.1
General
Under certain conditions, some kinds of discontinuous disturbances are exempted from the
definition of a click and the measurement procedure shall be able to verify these occurrences.
Figure 6 is a flow chart that shows how to consider these conditions in the verification
procedure.
Even if not shown in the flow chart, the verification procedure of this subclause 5.4.3 shall be
followed when a second measurement is needed in order to apply the upper quartile method.
5.4.3.2
Individual switching operations
Individual switching operations are caused by infrequent operations of a switch which is part
of the equipment either by direct or remote activation.
NOTE These switching operations have the potential to cause discontinuous disturbances but are disregarded
because infrequent.
Examples of individual switching operations are those for:
a) the purpose of mains connection or disconnection only;
b)the purpose of programme selection only;
c) the control of energy or speed by switching between a limited number of fixed
positions;
d) the changing of the manual setting of a continuously adjustable control such as a
variable speed device forwater extraction or electronic thermostats;

===== 第 63 页 / 共 157 页 =====
Any disturbance caused by individual switching operations shall be disregarded for the
purpose of testing the EUT for compliance with the limits of radio disturbance set out in this
standard.
Examples of switches covered by this subclause are the on/off switches for apparatus
(including foot activated), manual switches for heat and airflow control in fan heaters and hair
dryers, as well as the indirectly operated switch in a cupboard, wardrobe or refrigerator, and
sensor-operated switches,etc.
Also the disturbance caused by the operation of any switching device or control which is
included in an equipment for the purpose of mains disconnection for safety only, is to be

Operating conditions
6.1
General
The EuT shall be tested when operated from the intended power supply sources according to
6.2 and/or 6.3as appropriate.
Unless in conflict with the manufacturer's instructions, the operating and/or load conditions for
test shall be as defined in Annex A. If Annex A does not define operating modes and/or load
conditions the equipment shall be tested in all the relevant operating modes. Where there is a
conflict, the manufacturer's instructions shall take precedence.
Normal load conditions shall be as defined in 6.2, 6.3 and Annex A, unless these are in
conflict with the manufacturer's instruction for use, which in such cases take precedence.
Where the EUT is not covered by these subclauses,the manufacturer's instruction for use
shall be followed.
The duration of operation is not restricted unless the manufacturer specifies limitations for the
operating time of the EUT.In this case the limitations shall be complied with.
No running-in time to be specified but, prior to testing, the EuT shall be operated for a
sufficient period to ensure that the conditions of operation will be typical of those during
normal life of the equipment. Running-in of motors shall be carried out by the manufacturer.
The ambient temperature shall lie within the range 15 °C to 35 °C.

speed controls shall be adjusted to approximately maximum speed and mid-range speed, and

Once the setting of controls, which are not intended for frequent adjustment in normal use,
has been pre-set by the manufacturer, it shall not be further adjusted during the test.
6.5
Multifunction equipment
Multifunction equipment which is subjected simultaneously, to different, clauses of this
standard and/or other standards shall be tested with each function operated in isolation, if this
can be achieved without modifying the equipment internally. The equipment thus tested shall
be deemed to have complied with the requirements of all clauses/standards when each
function has satisfied the requirements of the relevant clause/standard.
For equipment for which it is not practical to test with each function operated in isolation, or
its primary function, the equipment shall be deemed to have complied only if it meets the
provisions of each clause/standard with the necessary functions operative.

InterpretationofCisPRradiodisturbancelimits
7.1
Significance of a CISPR limit
A CisPR limit is a limit recommended to national authorities for incorporation in national
standards, relevant legal regulations and official specifications. It is also recommended that
international organizationsusetheselimits.
The significance of the limits for type approved equipment shall be that on a statistical basis
at least 80 % of the mass-produced equipment complies with the limits with at least 80 %
confidence.
In the case of discontinuous disturbance when the shortened procedure described in 7.2.2.2
is applied, compliance with the limits on the 8o % -8o %basis is not guaranteed.
7.2
Typetests
7.2.1
Equipment producing continuous disturbance

===== 第 69 页 / 共 157 页 =====
Type tests shall be made either:
a) on a sample of_equipment of the type using the statistical method of evaluation in
accordance with 7.3,or
b) for simplicity's sake, on one unit only.
Subsequent tests are necessary from time to time on equipment taken at random from the
production, especially if option b) above has been followed.
7.2.2
Equipment producing discontinuous disturbance
7.2.2.1
Type tests shall be made on one unit only.
Subsequent tests are necessary from time to time on units taken at random from the
production.
7.2.2.2
In the case of controversy with regard to a type approval test, the following
shortened procedure is applied:
If the first unit is tested and fails, three additional units shall be tested at the same frequency
or frequencies at which the first unit failed.
The three additional units are judged according to the same requirements as applied to the
first unit.
If all three additional units comply with the relevant requirements, the type is approved.
If one or more units do not comply, the type is rejected.

methods described below or to some other test which ensures compliance with the
requirements of 7.1.
The test according to 7.3.2 or 7.3.3 should be performed on a sample of not less than 5 items
of the type,but if, in exceptional circumstances, 5 items are not available,then a sample of at
least 3 shall be used.
The test according to 7.3.4 should be performed on a sample of not less than 7 items.

if the plug or socket of the leads is easily replaceable by the user. The measurement shall be

than O,4 m or if connected directly by plug and socket to the vacuum cleaner they shall be
measured together. In all other cases, the EUT shall be measured separately.

Floor polishers
Floor polishers shall be operated continuously without any mechanical load on the polishing
brushes.
A.1.3
Coffee grinders and coffee makers
A.1.3.1
Coffee grinders
Coffee grinders shall be operated continuously without load.
Coffee grinders with a timer shall be operated without load for the maximum duration allowed
by the timer.
Coffee grinders without a timer shall be operated without load for the duration taken to grind
the maximum quantity of roasted coffee beans stated in the instructions.
If it is not possible to operate the grinder without load, the grinder shall be operated using the
maximum quantity of roasted coffee beans stated in the instructions.
A.1.3.2
Coffee makers and espresso makers with integrated grinder
Coffee makers and espresso makers with integrated grinder shall be tested according to 6.5.
The grinder function shall be tested according to A.1.3.1.
If the operation time of the coffee grinder can be set by the user, it should be set to maximum
duration.
A.1.3.3
Fullyautomaticcoffeemakers
Fully automatic coffee makers shall be tested according to 6.5. The different functions shall
be tested sequentially so that all possible disturbance sources are covered.
The test conditions shall reflect the normal operation of the equipment, as stated in the
shall be tested:
keep warm mode forfully automated coffee makers;
pre-heating for espresso coffee makers;

Ventilation fans shall be operated continuously with maximum airflow. If an electronic control

Extractor and range hoods shall be operated continuously with maximum airflow. If an

A.1.9
Refrigeratorsandfreezers
Refrigerators and freezers shall be operated continuously with the door closed. The
thermostat shall be adjusted to the middle of the adjustment range. The cabinet shall be
empty and not heated. The measurement shall be made after the steady state has been
reached.
The light inside the cabinet shall be switched off during the measurement, unless it can be
switched on by the user while the door is closed or it is continuously switched on during
normal operation.
If the clicks are not measured, the click rate N is determined from half the number of switching
operations.

A.1.10Washing machines
Washing machines shall be operated with water but without textiles, the temperature of the
incoming water shall be in accordance with the manufacturer's instruction for use.

For the evaluation of continuous disturbances, infrequent short term events are disregarded if
they do not last more than a few seconds, e.g. during the start of a spin cycle.
For the evaluation of discontinuous disturbances a complete program cotton 6o C without
prewash, if available, is measured, otherwise the regular wash program without prewash is
used.
NOTE For machines where the drying function forms a part of the programme, see A.1.12 or A.1.13.

and measurements need not be made on the lead to these valves.

Dish washers shall be operated with water but without dishes. The temperature of the

Centrifugal dryers shall be operated continuously without load.

Razors and hair clippers shall be operated continuously without load, according to general

not sewing any material). See also A.10.1.2 or 6.4, where applicable.

The ambient temperature is defined at the temperature of the air flow to the indoor unit.
A.1.20.4If the equipment consists of indoor and outdoor units (split type) the length of

CISPR14-1:2016IEC2016
-65-
to approximate a circular shape having a diameter of approximately (1 ± 0,3) m. If the pipe
length cannot be adjusted, it shall be longer than 4 m, but not longer than 8 m.
For the measurement of disturbance power on the connecting leads between the two units,
the leads shall be separated from the refrigerant pipe and extended to accommodate the
clamp. For all other measurements of disturbance power and disturbance voltage the
connecting leads between the two units shall be routed along the refrigerant pipe. Where an
earthing conductor is required, but not included in the mains lead, the earthing terminal of the
outdoor unit shall be connected to the reference ground (see 5.2.1, 5.2.2 and 5.2.3).
For disturbance voltage measurement the AMN shall be situated at a distance of o,8 m from
the unit (either the indoor or outdoor unit) which is connected to the AC mains network.
Alternatively for the measurement of disturbance voltages or disturbance power, the test set-
up in A.1.20.5 may be used.
In order to determine the starting frequency of the disturbance voltage or disturbance current
test on ports other than the AC mains, if no specific information about the length of the
connecting leads is given by the manufacturer, it shall be assumed that their length is always
greater than 2 m but less than 30 m.
When the disturbance current probe method is selected to measure the disturbance from
leads other than the mains routed along the refrigerant pipe, all leads and all refrigerant pipes
and not the pipes may be clamped.

-If the tool is sold together with an EPs, the disturbance shall be assessed by

Warming plates, boiling tables, heating drawers and heating cabinets shall be operated with
no load in the heating compartment or on the heating surface.

General

once the EUT has returned to a standby rest state.If the number of clicks produced by each

sixth of the number of clicks produced in a single dispensing operation. If the number of clicks
and the click rate N shall be determined from at least 40 clicks on the assumption that the rest
period between each dispensing operation was such that the 10 operations were uniformly
distributed over a period of one hour. The rest period is to be included in the minimum
observationtime.

===== 第 120 页 / 共 157 页 =====
Video machines and other similar equipment shall be operated in accordance with the
manufacturer's instruction for use. The operating cycle shall be the programme obtained after
inserting the largest number of coins with the minimum value necessary to start the EUT.
Where it is possible to select several programmes, the programme giving the maximum click
rate shall be selected. Should the duration of the programme be less than 1 min, the following
programme is not to be started within one minute off the start of the previous programme so
as to reflect normal use. This rest period is to be included in the minimum observation time.
The programme shall be repeated as often as necessary to produce a minimum of 4o clicks.

A.7
Electricandelectronictoys
A.7.1
Classification
For the purposes of this standard, toys are subdivided into categories.
For each category specific requirements are given.
Category A: Battery toys without active electronic circuits or motors.
NOTE 1Examples are electric torches for children.
Category B: Battery toys with built-in batteries, without possibility for external electric
connection.
NOTE 2Examples are musical soft toys, educational computers or motorised toys.
Category C:Battery toys having associated units which are, or can be, connected by means
of an electric cord.
NOTE 3Examples are cord-controlled toys and telephone sets.
NOTE 4Examples of associated units are battery boxes, control units and headphones.
Category D: Transformer toys and dual supply toys incorporating no active electronic circuits.

without electronic controls.

toys which are not covered by the other categories are also included in this category.
NOTE 6 Examples are educational computers, electric organs and chess sets and track sets with electronic
control units.
For toys running on tracks, disturbance power measurements may be used as an alternative
to radiateddisturbance measurement.

connected to the earth terminal of the AMN. The earth terminal of the load, if any, is
connected to the earth terminal of the external power controllers, or, if not available, directly
to the earth terminal of the AMN.
The external power controllers shall be tested first on the mains port in accordance with the
provisions of 5.2.1 and 5.2.2.1.Secondly,measurements of the disturbance voltage or
disturbance current shall be made at associated ports using a probe selected between those
described in 5.1.4 and 5.1.5.
